dialog.body: Public Works, this is Denise. How can I help you?
Hi, yes, good morning. It's Sal Barone. I'm calling about the plow, um, they came down my street and left a, a pile across the driveway. A big hard ridge of it.
Okay, Mr. Barone, I'm sorry about that. What's the address?
Two-oh-one Harrison Avenue. Over on the Fort Adams side. We share the driveway with the people next door, so it's across the whole thing, both of us, it's...
Got it, two-oh-one Harrison. So the plow came through and pushed a berm across the end of the shared driveway. Is that right?

Yes, that's it. Right across. And it's not soft, it's heavy, because of the rain on top of it. That storm last weekend, the snow and then it turned to rain, Sunday into Monday, and now it's all packed and froze up.
Yeah, that stuff turns to cement. Has anyone been able to get a car in or out?
No. No, nobody's going anywhere. I did a little with the shovel yesterday but I'm eighty-something, I can't be... [pause] Hold on a second.
No, honey, in a minute. I said in a minute. Go sit down. Sorry, my youngest is here and he wants a snack, he's asked me about every thirty seconds since eight o'clock.
That's all right, go ahead and take care of him if you need to.
No, no, he's fine. He can wait. Where was I. The berm. Yeah, so I'm annoyed, I'll be honest, because it's the same thing every time. They clear the street nice and the driveway gets buried.

I understand. It's frustrating, you clear the whole thing and then the plow undoes it. Let me put in a request for a crew to come back and clear the end of the driveway. I can't tell you exactly when, they're still working through a lot of calls from the storm.

Yeah. Okay. Well, any time today would be... [trailing] And, um, the other thing is it's all ice now, the walkway and the end of the drive. Can somebody bring sand? Or is there a place I can get some?

I can add a note asking for sand at that location. Also, I can tell you there are usually sand piles the city puts out for residents, but let me check where the nearest one is for you. Can you hold for a moment?
Sure, I'll hold.

Mr. Barone, thanks for waiting. I checked with the yard. Residents can pick up a bucket's worth of sand at the public works yard, but I know with the ice you're not driving anywhere. So I've noted on the request that you need sand delivered or put down at the driveway.
Okay. That's, that's good. I can't lift a bucket anyway. [pause] Sorry, what, honey? A cracker. Give him a cracker, Denise, I mean, sorry, no, I'm talking to him. Hold on.
Take your time.
Okay. He got the crackers. So, the sand, and the berm. Is there a number or something I can write down?
I'll give you my name, it's Denise, and you can call this same department line and mention the request for Harrison Avenue. Do you want me to confirm your callback number?
It's four-oh-one, five-five-five, oh-one-six-three.

Four-oh-one, five-five-five, oh-one-six-three. That's what I have. And just to read it back, two-oh-one Harrison Avenue, berm across the shared driveway, needs clearing, and sand for the walkway and the end of the drive.
That's right. Thank you. I hope somebody comes today, because the neighbor's going to ask me again, and I, I don't...
I hear you. I've marked it so the crew supervisor sees it this afternoon. If it gets dark and nobody's been, call back and ask for me.
Okay. Okay, thank you, Denise. Bye now.
Bye, Mr. Barone. Take care.
